title: Doors & Hardware
short_answer: The frame decides everything. Set it plumb, square, and the right width, anchored to real framing — and the door hangs and latches.
summary: Get the frame right and the rest is easy. Both jambs plumb, head level, throat correct, anchored at the frame's anchor points. If a door won't latch, the problem is almost always the frame.
plain_words: Get the frame right and the rest is easy. Both jambs plumb, the head level, the throat the right width, and anchored where the frame is made to be anchored. Keep the spreader on the bottom until it is fastened so the frame cannot pinch in. Then hang the door, fit hardware off the template, and adjust the closer last.
when_to_use: Setting hollow metal frames in steel stud walls during framing
Hanging doors and installing hardware per schedule
Rated or accessible openings — listed assembly and drawing dimensions
prerequisites: Door and frame schedule (not plan alone)
Scope confirmed: frames only vs full hardware — see provenance

materials.name: Door, hinges, lockset, closer per hardware set
Grout fill when schedule or label requires

steps.title: Door and frame schedule
steps.body: Work off the door and frame schedule — size, handing, frame type, throat depth, label, and hardware prep. Never off the plan alone.

steps.title: Rough opening
steps.body: Confirm rough opening is frame dimension plus manufacturer's clearance.

steps.title: Plumb and level
steps.body: Set frame, plumb both jambs, level the head, check throat width at top, middle, and bottom.

steps.title: Spreader
steps.body: Leave shipping spreader on the bottom until the frame is anchored so jambs cannot pull in.

steps.title: Anchor
steps.body: Anchor at the frame's own anchor locations into jamb studs — not wherever is convenient.

steps.title: Diagonals
steps.body: Check diagonals. A frame can be plumb and level and still be racked.

steps.title: Grout
steps.body: Grout-fill where the schedule or label requires it.

steps.title: Protect frame
steps.body: Protect the frame — a dented frame at a main entrance is a replacement, not a repair.

steps.title: Hang and hardware
steps.body: Install order: hinges, lock or latch, closer, stop and silencers. Use manufacturer template for every prep. Adjust closer last.

steps.title: Opening done
steps.body: Frame plumb/square, door latches without push/pull, gaps consistent, hardware set complete, rated labels legible with no field mods, accessible clearances per drawings.

warnings.title: Connects to our framing
warnings.body: Hollow metal frames in steel stud walls get set while the wall is being framed and anchor into jamb studs we build. Rough opening, jamb stud detail, and anchor locations are part of the framing pass.

warnings.title: Rated openings
warnings.body: Door, frame, hardware, and gasketing are one listed assembly. Labels must stay legible. No field modification of labeled door or frame — wrong prep is a supplier problem.

warnings.title: Scope question for GVC
warnings.body: Doors & Hardware is title-only in the portal estimate scope catalog. Before pricing, confirm: frames only vs hang and hardware; furnish vs install-only; keying and closer adjustment ownership. Setting frames and installing finish hardware are very different scopes.

experts.tag: Full detail · labeled openings and ADA
experts.summary: Rated: whole opening is one assembly — labels legible, no field mods, self-closing and positive-latching, limited undercut, wall around opening rated too. Accessibility: clear width, maneuvering clearance per approach, opening force, lever hardware height, threshold limits, closer timing — exact numbers from project drawings, not memory. Hardware: work from hardware sets; confirm handing; template every prep; adjust closer last; verify full swing clearance.

quality_checks.prompt: Work from door/frame schedule — not plan guess
Frame plumb, level, square, correct throat, anchored at frame points
Door latches without being pushed or pulled
Rated openings: labels legible, no field mods, self-closing/latching verified

common_mistakes.title: Plan-only sizing
common_mistakes.wrong: Size frame from floor plan without schedule
common_mistakes.right: Door and frame schedule is SoT

common_mistakes.title: Remove spreader early
common_mistakes.right: Spreader stays until frame is anchored
common_mistakes.why: Pinched jambs — door never latches right

common_mistakes.title: Field mod on labeled door
common_mistakes.wrong: Drill new prep in labeled door or frame

common_mistakes.title: Adjust lock instead of frame
common_mistakes.wrong: Fight hardware when frame is racked
common_mistakes.why: Latch problems are usually frame problems

troubleshooting.symptom: Door will not latch without force
troubleshooting.likely_cause: Frame racked, jambs not plumb, or spreader removed early
troubleshooting.fix: Re-check diagonals and throat; re-anchor before hardware fight

troubleshooting.likely_cause: Frame not level/plumb or wrong hinge adjustment
troubleshooting.fix: Level head and jambs; shim hinges only after frame is true

provenance.note: Frame setting, spreader use, anchoring at frame anchor locations, and hardware install order are standard hollow metal and door hardware practice; manufacturer instructions govern specifics. Rated requirements come from individual listings and applicable codes — no field modification of labeled assemblies. Accessibility dimensions deliberately omitted here — take from project drawings.
